description: The tables the 'Restricted Content Owner' role holds Read on, at User (Basic) depth, so that Dataverse accepts the memberless 'Spaarke Restricted Content Owners' team as the OWNER of an ordinary row of the hard-deny tables (owner round 131, the 086 ruling; RecordOwnershipResolver.RestrictedContentTableSet). The team is created PER CUSTOMER business unit: in each customer's top business unit, the direct child of the root that provisioning H10 creates (customerBusinessUnitId, a sibling of Secure Record), never in the root, which holds only Spaarke product data (owner round 136). The role is created once in the root (Dataverse copies it into every child unit) and each customer unit's copy is assigned to that unit's team. Dataverse refuses an owner whose roles lack Read on the table ('Read Privilege Check For Owner failed ... is missing prv<Read> privilege'), and the BFF refuses the write with record_owner_restricted_content_team_unresolved when the answer's business unit is the root itself or sits under Secure Record, or the team in the customer's top unit is missing, ambiguous or has a member. This file is the ONE list. scripts/Set-RestrictedContentOwnerTeam.ps1 and RestrictedContentOwnerRoleGuardTests read it. Do not copy it anywhere else.
howToExtend: The tables are exactly RecordOwnershipResolver.RestrictedContentTables. Add or remove a table there first (an owner ruling), then here; RestrictedContentOwnerRoleGuardTests fails the build while the two differ.

'privilegeName' is the Read privilege's name from metadata (EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='x')/Privileges, PrivilegeType eq 'Read'). The casing follows the schema name. The script checks it against metadata and refuses a mismatch.

Then run, for each customer top business unit: scripts/Set-RestrictedContentOwnerTeam.ps1 -EnvironmentUrl <url> -CustomerBusinessUnitName <name> (or -CustomerBusinessUnitId <id>) (dry run), then -Apply (owner go), then -Verify.

Never add a depth, an access type or a member here. The role grants Read at User (Basic) depth and nothing else; the team has no members, ever, and holds no other role. Ordinary rows of these tables sit in the customer's top business unit, so no user-facing role may grant Read on them at a depth that reaches that unit from where its holder is homed outside an admin path: Organization depth reaches them for every holder, Deep (Parent: Child) for a holder homed in that unit or above it (the root), Business Unit depth only for a holder homed in that unit; a holder homed in a unit BELOW it does not reach them with Deep or Business Unit (task 191).

tables.reason: Owner round 131 (the 086 ruling): a rule's ordinary answer is this team, in place of a business unit's default team (RecordOwnershipResolver.OrdinaryExitAsync). An Unsecure moves a team-owned rule out of isolation to it, and the ordinary pass moves a rule still on a default team to it (SecureChildReconciler, R4b-2). An author-owned rule keeps its author (rule 1).
tables.evidence: No refusal of its own is recorded: the probe is a Dataverse write, made only after the owner's go (the team does not exist yet). Read-only, spaarkedev1, 2026-10-28: metadata names the table's Read privilege prvReadsprk_Policy (Id=eda1df58-8428-4b7a-827c-d9c9ebf6140f); no team named 'Spaarke Restricted Content Owners' and no role named like 'Restricted Content' exists. Dataverse refuses an owner team that lacks it with the 'Read Privilege Check For Owner failed ... is missing prv<Read> privilege' check config/secure-record-owner-role.json records verbatim for sprk_policyversion and sprk_invoice.

tables.reason: Owner round 131: a rule version follows its rule (sprk_policyversion.sprk_policy); its ordinary answer is this team, so the reconciler moves a team-owned version to it as it does the rule. OntologyAdminAuthoringService's publish binds no owner on an ordinary answer, so a published version stays its author's (rule 1).
tables.evidence: No refusal of its own is recorded (probe after the owner's go).
